name: Eleven Point River Dispersed Primitive Camping - Mark Twain National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Eleven Point Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general forest dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general national forest lands at least 100ft from roads, trails, and water bodies.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in organic soil, at least 200 feet from Eleven Point River and springs. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Missouri Department of Conservation burn bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved gravel forest service roads (FS 3152 / FS 4112)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Winding gravel forest roads with small washboards and dips.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main gravel forest roads in dry weather)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE on ridge turnouts; weak down near river bottom
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Ozark bluff river valleys restrict cell signals)

amenities: Spring-fed River Access (Eleven Point River - filter required)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-70°F, high spring river flow, blooming dogwoods, spring rainstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (85-92°F), spring-fed river float trips, high insect activity.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular Ozark autumn foliage (55-70°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), ideal camping weather.

dangers_and_hazards: Flash flooding along river drainages after heavy Ozark rain
Venomous snakes: Copperheads active in warm months

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional canoeist paddling on Eleven Point River

common_animals: Ozark Hellbender (Cryptobranchus alleganiensis bishopi - endangered aquatic salamander)

human_demographics_and_culture: Canoe floats / kayakers, Ozark Trail backpackers, trout anglers, and digital nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Osage indigenous traditions revere the crystal-clear karst springs (Greer Spring) and river bluffs of the Eleven Point basin as sacred life waters.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound karst spring vitality, soothing river acoustics, peaceful Ozark hill energy.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Scenic bluffs, spring branches, hardwood forests, river views

public_reviews_summary: Beautiful free primitive camping along the National Wild & Scenic Eleven Point River. Clean sites and good cell service on higher ridge turnouts.
other_data: Bortle Class 2-3 night sky. Abundant firewood.

name: Paddy Creek Wilderness Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: US Forest Service - Mark Twain National Forest (Houston Ranger District)

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - USFS Wilderness Primitive Camping (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed wilderness camping permitted throughout Paddy Creek Wilderness. Camp 100ft minimum from trails and streams.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway to gravel Forest Service roads (FR 220)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Graded gravel access roads, flat trailhead parking.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Accessible by standard 2WD low clearance vehicles.

nomad_connectivity_rating.overall_rating: Fair to Moderate / Ozark Ridge Signal
nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE on high forest ridges
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate in deep Ozark stream hollows

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 52-70°F, blooming dogwood and redbuds, spring stream flows.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 78-92°F, warm Ozark summer weather, shaded oak forest canopy.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 28-48°F, crisp clear winter air, light snowfall.

dangers_and_hazards: Flash flooding in creek hollows during thunderstorms
Ticks and chiggers in summer (use permethrin)

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 9/10 - Creek water trickles and Ozark woodland birds

human_demographics_and_culture: Osage ancestral lands, Ozark mountain locals, Missouri backpackers, nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Rich Ozark mountain folklore honoring the ancient pine hollows and crystal spring waters of Texas County.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Peaceful Ozark ridge solitude, pristine pine hollow air.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Sandstone bluffs, pine ridges, pristine creek crossings

public_reviews_summary: Ozark wilderness primitive camping at its finest. Free USFS access, serene pine ridges, and easy drive to Houston and Rolla.
other_data: Mark Twain National Forest. Free wilderness dispersed camping.
